A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Finite Group|finite group]] and $H$ a [[Definition:Subgroup|subgroup]] of $G$.
Then:
:$\order G = \order H \index G H$
where $\index G H$ is the [[Definition:Index of Subgroup|index]] of $H$ in $G$.

B_source.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Finite Group|finite group]] which [[Definition:Group Action|acts]] on a set $X$, and let $x \in X$.
Then:
:$\order G = \card {\Orb x} \order {\Stab x}$

substitutions.group action: action of G on left cosets G/H by left multiplication

validity_conditions: G acts transitively on G/H by left multiplication, so the orbit of the coset H is all of G/H, of size [G:H].
The stabilizer of the coset H under this action is exactly H, so |Stab| = |H|.
proof_plan: Let $G$ act on the [[Definition:Left Coset Space|left coset space]] $G / H$ by $g * \paren {a H} = \paren {g a} H$.

The [[Definition:Stabilizer|stabilizer]] of the coset $H$ is:
:$\set {g \in G: g H = H} = H$
The [[Definition:Orbit (Group Theory)|orbit]] of $H$ is $\set {g H: g \in G} = G / H$, of size $\index G H$.
